note: Public sanitized view: job names, static descriptions, health, and freshness only. No paths/errors.

jobs.description: The 15-minute heartbeat of your Chief of Staff. Every cycle it gathers each job's status, runs the monitors, and refreshes this dashboard.
The once-a-day deeper pass (10:30 PM). It re-checks every pipeline, pre-computes tomorrow's watch schedule, and writes the nightly prep report.
Retired Tier 2 local calendar writer. Disabled during a 30-day evidence gate; Google Apps Script Tier 1 is the sole writer and CalendarAudit supplies the read-only shadow detector.
Your weekly AI-power-user briefing — calendar, recent reading, action items, and ideas in one email. Curated from the week's activity.
Weekly Fresh in Your Fridge menu classifier that renders Miele reheat guidance and emails Eric and Jung.
Daily 2 AM private event-discovery pull for find-us-an-event; refreshes the flagship Vibe Finder board.
Weekly curation of tips and insights from your own follow-ups and ideas backlog. Surfaces patterns worth acting on.
Every 30 minutes, checks that your Google and Gmail logins are alive. The early-warning system for the auth failures that quietly break your pipelines.

jobs.display_name: AI Chief of Staff Deployment Drift
jobs.description: Hourly check that the Chief of Staff's live code has no uncommitted changes (matches the committed git baseline). Catches accidental or unreviewed changes to the monitor itself.
An independent, out-of-band guard that asks 'is the Chief of Staff alive?' every hour. If the heartbeat goes stale it emails you — built so it can't die the same way the monitor would.
A read-only health probe of your Codex tool — context bloat, database growth, stale workspaces. Watching and recording for now; it doesn't alert yet.
A read-only health probe of Claude Code itself — history, connectors, hooks. Watching and recording for now; it doesn't alert yet.
Reads each tick for jobs that need attention and sends one de-duplicated alert. It only notifies — it never tries to fix things itself.
A weekly deep diagnostic of your machine — orphaned processes, memory bloat, messy config, stale plugins. The thorough tune-up beyond the quick daily check.
Each morning it re-checks your open follow-ups to confirm they actually resolved, then closes or flags them. It also tracks the self-healing engine's health over a rolling week.
A weekly audit of the email-to-calendar pipeline. For 13 known booking senders it checks how many emails should have become events but silently didn't, and emails you if the miss rate climbs.
Each week it reads ~20 security sources for new threats to your AI tools, then checks whether your setup is exposed. Your defensive early-warning.
The free 8:30 AM liveness check that auto-repairs small issues and produces your session-start warnings. The lightweight daily counterpart to the weekly deep scan.
Hourly mirror of your irreplaceable files to the D: drive. An always-current local copy.
A daily point-in-time snapshot to the D: drive, keeping ~21 days of history. Lets you roll back to a specific day, not just the latest.
Daily backup of your Claude Code setup to OneDrive cloud storage. Your off-machine copy.
Hourly commit-and-push of your workstation configuration to a private GitHub repo. Keeps your machine's recovery setup versioned and safe.
Nightly zip backup of AI tools configuration to the replacement backup target after the OneDrive sync remediation.
Hourly backup of the Chief of Staff's own code to a private remote. The safety net for the monitor itself (recently repaired).

Hourly publisher that copies the sanitized health board to Eric's public apps site so his phone can read it. This tile watches the published copy itself — if the publisher dies, the phone board goes stale and this tile names the culprit.

Daily read-only canary for the on-demand produce-cart skill. Verifies the shared seasonal-produce calendar loads, covers the current season, and its ranking logic still picks fresh items — no cart, browser, email, or LLM involved.

Daily read-only canary for the Cupcake Tracker PWA (Railway). Plain GET of the app shell plus /api/health — requires 200, the app's title marker, and a healthy backend; never logs in or writes tracker state.

Daily read-only canary for the chore-tracker app 'Nest Maintenance' (Railway). Plain GET of the app shell plus /api/health — requires 200, the app's title marker, and a healthy backend; never creates, completes, or edits chores.

Daily read-only canary for the Pantry Shelf PWA (GitHub Pages private tile). Plain GET requiring 200 plus the app's title marker, proving the real app shell rendered rather than a generic host page; never touches inventory data.

Daily read-only canary for the private browser-debate delivery path (debate-share on Railway). GET /health (no auth) plus GET /auth-check with the local User-scope DEBATE_SHARE_TOKEN — exercises the exact upload auth logic without creating a slug, writing /data, or exposing any token material (presence booleans + HTTP verdicts only). Catches a broken service, missing local token, or token mismatch BEFORE the next debate finale fails at publish time.

Daily read-only canary for the Debate Runner v15 watcher itself (email -> spawned-agent browser debates, C:\code\debate-runner). Checks the DebateRunner-Watcher scheduled task is Ready/Running, watch.log advanced within 15 min (with an in-flight-debate exemption via browser.lock — one tick blocks 1-2h for a whole debate by design), and surfaces an active pause (tripwire / DEBATE STOP kill switch) as watching. This is the dead-watcher detector: the watcher's own failure alerts ride the same gws auth it needs alive, so when IT dies, only this canary notices.
